paragraphs.text: Good afternoon, elders and sisters. Well, I hope you had a good, restful Sabbath, and you've had a productive prep day so far.

As I said earlier in the text that should have gone out to all of you, you don't need to do all your shopping for the week on prep day anymore. You can shop every day of the week except for Sunday for all the essential needs that you have.

For your water, for your food, things like that, just go out and get those things as you need them. Make sure you're getting some fresh fruit and some vegetables and getting those things when they're fresh on the day. Use them on the day or use them over a couple of days, and that way you don't need to worry quite so much about carrying so much, especially if just one of you is able to leave the apartment.

Remember to save your 14-day food supply for when you might really need it. That's not for you to eat right now. If any of you don't have a 14-day food supply or you don't have the three bottles of water per missionary, please let me know so we can get those to you as soon as possible.

We don't know. We're hoping things get better, but if for some reason we get to a place where we can't get out for several days, we're going to be fine because we're prepared. You know what the scripture says: if you're prepared, you shall not fear.

So hopefully we won't need to use that, but we want to keep it on hand just in case we do. So always keep your water topped up, and don't eat that food until you absolutely can't go out and get regular food on a day-to-day basis.

Now I'm hearing some great reports about your video, audio, and chat ministering. The members are loving your proactive outreach and service. I'm getting some calls from bishops and stake presidents because you're lifting hearts and lifting spirits, so keep it going.

The more consistent you are, the more effective you will become and the more people you'll reach and bless. I always remember that quantity precedes quality. We just can't get good until we do something a lot. So the more we do of something, the better we get at it.
The key to this is we want to get good at it because it blesses more lives the better we are at it, and it blesses our lives the better we get at it.

Now as an update, our North American fellow missionaries all got home on Sunday. They'll be in a 14-day quarantine. I've heard from some of them already because they're probably going a little crazy in their apartments for 14 days, just like you kind of can be if you don't have your mission purpose focused in. But they're sad not to be here.
After the 14 days, many of them will be reassigned to a local mission. Most of our other international missionary colleagues are also home now and in their 14-day quarantine.

There's still a few of our fellow missionaries at the MTC, and they're waiting to get tickets to their home countries. But in some cases they may not be able to do that, and if that's the case, then we're hopeful that they'll be able to come and return to their service with us.
Now, elders and sisters, I continue to be inspired by your faithfulness and your valiance. You are remarkable young people with unlimited potential and a hugely bright future before you.

Remind yourself often that this will pass, and life will get back to a more normal routine soon enough. The key is to use this time wisely so that when things get back to normal, you'll feel gratitude about the way you used your time and energy during maybe the greatest test of your mission. Love y'all. Talk to you tomorrow.
